evidence: LC n79051222 identifies John R. Clarke (born 1945), author of Roman Black-and-White Figural Mosaics and the Roman art books. LC n80046209 identifies James Franklin Clarke (1906-1982), the Bulgarian historian with a 1938 PhD. These are distinct people and careers, not duplicate authorities.

LC no2001005892 is William Jackson Coleman (born 1911), credited with Latin-American Catholicism; n79150298 is William Robert Coleman (1934-1988), historian of science whose Harvard dissertation on Cuvier dates to 1962. The 1950 papal-policy dissertation and the Cuvier/biology books belong to different people.

LC n87932055 is James B. Collins, Georgetown historian of French taxation; n80045215 is John Joseph Collins (born 1946), Yale biblical scholar. They are distinct. In addition, b mixes the biblical books with Edmund John Collins’s Jazz Feedback to Africa and highlife research; its 1955 Caesar article also predates the biblical scholar’s adulthood.

LC no2014089427 identifies Grace Davie (born 1974), Queens College African historian and author of Poverty Knowledge in South Africa. LC n90685299 identifies Grace Riestra Claire Davie (born 1946), Exeter sociologist associated with Religion in Britain since 1945. Separate people, not duplicate records.

a combines James Barker Farr’s maritime work (A Slow Boat to Nowhere, also a chapter title in Black Odyssey) with James R. Farr’s French Catholic-Reformation research and political scientist James Farr’s Locke article. b is James Barker Farr, the Black Odyssey author (LC n88194470); only part of a belongs to him.

LC nr95017510 identifies Sarah Barringer Gordon (born 1955), author of The Mormon Question; n80127208 identifies Sarah Herbert Gordon (born 1950), author of A Society of Passengers. These are distinct people, but a also contains the 1975 Smith College Students article, explicitly credited by its publisher to Sarah H. Gordon, contaminating a with b’s work.

LC n2002089928 identifies Michael Johnston Grant (born 1961), author of Down and Out on the Family Farm. LC n79150358 identifies Michael Grant (1914-2004), classical historian and author of From Imperium to Auctoritas. The Great Plains rehabilitation dissertation/book and the Roman history books represent different careers.

LC n83205669 is archivist and stagecoach historian Oliver W. Holmes (1902-1981); n79054782 is Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. (1841-1935), a distinct person. b combines the justice’s Common Law and correspondence with the archivist’s stagecoach articles, including Shall Stagecoaches Carry the Mail? (1963), also represented in a as a later book.

LC n85016398 identifies Kristin Mann (born 1946), Emory historian and author of Marrying Well, matching the Lagos dissertation and slavery research. LC n2009072279 identifies Kristin Dutcher Mann (born 1972), author of The Power of Song, matching the northern New Spain dissertation. Different people and coherent, separate publication histories.

The initials-only a aggregates multiple authors: Seneca the Satirist (1945) is by J. M. K. Martin, La Pouille (1993) by Jean-Marie Martin, and the Protestant separatism article by J. W. Martin. b is Janet Louise Block Martin (born 1945; LC n85334272), whose 1980 fur-trade dissertation developed into Treasure of the Land of Darkness. a is not one career.

LC n90650793 identifies Charles Gregg Singer (1910-1999), with a 1940 University of Pennsylvania PhD on South Carolina and later church-history work. LC n79054769 identifies Charles Joseph Singer (1876-1960), historian of medicine and science, author of Studies in the History and Method of Science and A History of Technology. Distinct authorities and careers.

LC n96034774 is nutrition historian David F. Smith (born 1954); n84804828 is Maine/H. G. Wells historian David Clayton Smith (1929-2009), distinct people. a mixes nutrition books with David Kammerling Smith’s Structuring Politics and a 1911 article impossible for its anchored author. b also includes David Chan Smith’s 2018 Hudson’s Bay Company article. Neither key is a clean single-person bundle.

The LC records distinguish two Andrew Stuart Thompsons: n99046183 (born 1968), author of Imperial Britain and The Empire Strikes Back?, and no2007021362 (born 1975), Waterloo PhD writing on human rights and international governance. The British empire books and Canadian NGO dissertation/books belong to different scholars despite identical full names.

a’s modern-history articles are credited by Cambridge to J. A. Thompson, including the 1973 William Appleman Williams article (St Catharine’s College, Cambridge). b is James Westfall Thompson (1869-1941; LC n79106105), whose 1895 French monarchy dissertation and medieval-history books form a much earlier career. Later reprints of b’s books do not make him the modern article author.

LC n79093584 identifies Richard White (born 1947), Stanford historian and author of Land Use, Environment, and Social Change, matching a’s 1975 dissertation and western/environmental books. LC n00012701 identifies Canadian Richard Wallace White (born 1952), whose Toronto dissertation on the Shanlys became Gentlemen Engineers. These are separate people and authorities.
